document.title: Taste Lab: fix a skill weakness with taps on a phone, not hand-written evals
document.summary: Adds Taste Lab, scripts that build a phone page of blind duels between eval runs and read the answers back, plus a no-vendor-lock-in rule in `AGENTS.md`.
document.why: In [PR #209](source:s1), the owner wants his taste in the skill and in review expectations, but never manages to hand-write evals or skill text.

sources.label: PR #209
sources.title: Taste Lab: fix a skill weakness with taps on a phone, not hand-written evals

parts.name: Taste Lab
parts.summary: Blind duels between eval runs, answered on a phone.

parts.name: No vendor lock-in
parts.summary: A project rule to build on git, files, and HTML.

groups.title: Duel cards from two reviews
groups.summary: `duelCards` in `cards.ts` pairs the pieces two reviews of one case wrote, and the test pins each pairing rule.

attention.note: `duelCards` writes a card only when both reviews wrote the piece and their words differ. Trace: side x has a `why` and side y has none, so no `why` card appears, and the tally never sees that y left it out. Decide whether a missing piece should duel against an empty side.

notes.body: `refCoversPath` is the directory rule `src/review/coverage.ts` also uses.

fileNotes.scripts/taste/cards.ts: New; pairs groups by shared paths, line notes within one line.
fileNotes.scripts/taste/cards.test.ts: Seven cases: skips, grouping text, directory refs, three-card cap.

groups.title: Rounds and answer codes
groups.summary: `round.ts` hashes the cards into a round id and reads the page's answer code back into picks and a tally.

attention.note: The code `taste.<id>.<duels>.<ideas>` is the only link between `page.html` and `readCode`. The id is the first 8 hex characters of a SHA-1 over every card text, so `readCode` refuses a code whose id, length, or letters do not match `round.json`. Duel letters are `x y s n -`; idea letters are `y n -`.

fileNotes.scripts/taste/round.ts: New; `tally` sorts by win rate, then wins, like the end screen.
fileNotes.scripts/taste/round.test.ts: Reads `xyns.y-` back; rejects wrong round, length, and letter.

groups.title: taste:page and taste:read commands
groups.summary: `run.ts` backs the two new `package.json` scripts: `page` builds a round from eval runs, and `read` decodes a code.

attention.note: When `TASTE_WEBHOOK_URL` is set in the environment or `.env`, `page` writes the URL into `index.html`, and the end screen posts the code to it. Anyone who opens a hosted copy can read the URL and post to it. The usage text and the skill say to keep such a page private; the code does not enforce it.

notes.body: `evalCacheDir` is `<git common dir>/comprehende-eval-cache`, so all worktrees share rounds.
`loadDotEnv` reads `.env` in this checkout, then in the main checkout.
The hex check stops a code from naming a path outside the rounds folder.

fileNotes.scripts/taste/run.ts: New; writes `index.html` and `round.json` per round id.

groups.title: The phone page
groups.summary: `page.html` shows each duel or idea card, keeps answers in `localStorage`, and ends on the answer code and a score.

attention.note: `answer` ignores a tap within 350 ms of a card showing, and the next card renders 170 ms after a pick. This stops the second tap of a double-tap from answering a card unseen, at the cost of dropping a fast deliberate tap.

notes.body: `run.ts` replaces `"__ROUND__"` with the round JSON, with `<` escaped.
Card ids end in a hex hash from `cards.ts`, so about half flip.

groups.title: The taste-lab agent skill
groups.summary: The `taste-lab` skill tells an agent the loop from a pinned issue to an applied fix, and `AGENTS.md` points to it.

fileNotes..agents/skills/taste-lab/SKILL.md: New internal skill: seven steps from issue to applied winner.

groups.title: No vendor lock-in rule
groups.why: [PR #209](source:s1) makes the page plain HTML so any harness can show it, and states this as a project rule.
groups.summary: `AGENTS.md` adds a project rule: build on git, files, and plain HTML, with T3 Code as the one assumed harness.

attention.note: The rule bans lock-in to one agent or provider, but names T3 Code as the one harness agents may assume. `page.html` already reads T3 Code theme variables first and falls back to system colors. Decide whether T3 Code is an allowed default or an exception the rule should not name.

commits.subject: Taste Lab: one self-contained page, no vendor store, built around fixing a skill issue
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The page is plain HTML with the round inside it, so any harness can show
it. Answers come back as a short code that pnpm taste:read turns into
picks. Rounds live in the shared git dir. The skill now runs issue,
ideas, test runs, duel, pick. AGENTS.md states the no vendor lock-in rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Taste Lab: review fixes
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Group matching counts a directory ref as covering its files. Line notes
pair with the nearest unused note, and their card id holds both lines.
A group card shows why and questions. An answer keeps both texts, a
failed save does not count, and a fresh card ignores a double-tap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Taste Lab: duel cards from two eval runs, a phone page to vote, and the loop skill
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Máté gives taste as taps on his phone instead of hand-written evals.
pnpm taste:cards pairs the pieces two eval runs wrote for the same cases.
The taste-lab skill tells an agent how to load duels, read picks,
propose rules that the picks support, and apply the approved ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

removed: [PR #209](source:s1) shows `taste.2430fd.xyxxxyxx.yy` as the page's code and as phone proof. At head, `makeRound` cuts the round id to 8 hex characters, as in the body's `round 4f95a994`, so the page never prints a 6-character id. The id grew in commit `47fbf59e`, and no source says the phone proof ran again after it.
Why does `tally` sort by net wins while the end screen sorts by win rate?
